rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec quarter-point hike ~97%, small half-point chance (Hercules); ECB Dec ~90%; BoE Dec ~84%; BoJ Dec ~84%; BoC Dec ~44%; RBA 4.85%
rows.read: A quarter-point December Fed hike is now all but fully priced, with a small chance of a half-point move back in the mix. The European Central Bank, Bank of England and Bank of Japan are all expected to hike in December as well. The Bank of Canada is the main doubt, and Governor Tiff Macklem speaks today.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: Germany Ifo Nov 90.6 (fcst 90.6, Oct 90.2); ADP weekly 21.0K (prior 23.8K); Japan Nov PMI mfg 53.7, services 50.5; Australia composite 46.1
rows.read: Germany's Ifo business mood rose for a seventh month to its highest in more than three years, though factories turned more cautious. A weekly US private hiring estimate cooled slightly. Australian firms are cutting output and jobs.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: Australia CPI Oct due Tue 6:30 PM CT (fcst 4.7% y/y, Sep 4.3%); US core PCE Oct due Wed 7:30 AM CT (fcst +0.3% m/m, 3.2% y/y); Tokyo core CPI Nov due Thu 5:30 PM CT (fcst 2.9%); Brent ~$86.8
rows.read: Inflation is still well above target almost everywhere, which keeps most central banks leaning toward hikes. Falling oil should ease some of that pressure in the months ahead. Australian inflation on Tuesday evening and US core inflation on Wednesday are the week's big tests.

rows.figure: Brent ~$86.81 (−1.88%), lowest since Aug 27 on Reuters; WTI ~$80.25; gold ~$3,628

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: Hedge funds (CFTC, Nov 17): USD index −1.3K (flipped short), EUR −76.6K, GBP +28.8K, JPY −23.8K, CHF −19.8K, CAD −72.1K, AUD +38.0K, NZD −23.6K; asset managers GBP −104.6K, AUD −182.7K, EUR +147.2K
rows.read: The latest weekly figures show hedge funds have turned slightly against the dollar, while still betting against the euro, the kiwi, the franc and, most strongly, the Canadian dollar. They still bet on the pound and the Aussie, where big long-term investors take the opposite side. Where the two groups disagree, a surprise could set off a fast unwind.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: US 10-year ~4.94% (Hercules); France composite PMI 46.2, a six-month low; ECB Financial Stability Review: France debt 119% of GDP, deficit 5.5%
rows.read: France's debts, flagged by the European Central Bank as a risk, weigh more now that its economy looks close to recession. Record US government borrowing keeps long-term US borrowing costs high, with the 10-year yield just under 5%.
